name: Update exact counters

# Keeps the exact (un-rounded) star/fork/contributor/follower numbers in the
# profile README fresh. Shields' dynamic badges round to "49.5k"; these are
# static badges whose values this job rewrites every 6 hours.

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "23 */6 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  refresh:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Fetch counts and rewrite README
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          STARS=$(gh api repos/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute --jq '.stargazers_count')
          FORKS=$(gh api repos/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute --jq '.forks_count')
          FOLLOWERS=$(gh api users/diegosouzapw --jq '.followers')
          CONTRIB=$(gh api "repos/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/contributors?per_page=1" -i \
            | grep -o 'page=[0-9]*>; rel="last"' | grep -o '[0-9]*' | head -1)
          # Fail closed: never write an empty/zero counter over a good one.
          for v in "$STARS" "$FORKS" "$FOLLOWERS" "$CONTRIB"; do
            case "$v" in ''|0) echo "suspicious counter value, aborting"; exit 1;; esac
          done
          sed -i \
            -e "s|badge/stars-[0-9]*-|badge/stars-${STARS}-|" \
            -e "s|badge/forks-[0-9]*-|badge/forks-${FORKS}-|" \
            -e "s|badge/contributors-[0-9]*-|badge/contributors-${CONTRIB}-|" \
            -e "s|badge/followers-[0-9]*-|badge/followers-${FOLLOWERS}-|" \
            README.md

      - name: Commit if changed
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if git diff --quiet README.md; then
            echo "counters unchanged"
            exit 0
          fi
          git config user.name "diegosouzapw"
          git config user.email "diegosouza.pw@gmail.com"
          git add README.md
          git commit -m "docs: refresh exact counters"
          git push

# Hi, I'm Diego 👋 I build open-source AI infrastructure and communities around practical developer tools. I'm the creator and lead maintainer of [OmniRoute](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute), a free, MIT-licensed AI gateway built in public with a global community of contributors. Counters refresh every six hours. The contributor badge counts GitHub-linked accounts, including bots; it excludes anonymous author records. [Dated impact and counting notes](COMMUNITY.md). ## 📌 Featured projects
OmniRoute
Free, MIT-licensed AI gateway. One endpoint for hundreds of providers, with quota-aware routing, fallback, and open protocols. Built in public with a global contributor community.
 OmniCopilot
Open-source VS Code extension connecting GitHub Copilot Chat to models available through OmniRoute. Model access and costs depend on your configured providers.
OmniGlyph
Cut your Claude bill 59–70% by rendering bulky LLM context as dense PNG pages — 100% read accuracy, exact per-provider billing math, fail-closed gates, measured benchmarks…
 OmniAntigravityRemoteChat
📱 Control your Antigravity AI sessions from your phone — real-time chat mirroring, multi-window management, and model switching via CDP
awesome-omni-skills
Public repository of AI coding skills, curated improved best-practice skills, and runtime surfaces for CLI, API, MCP, and A2A.
 ghostty-web
Ghostty for the web with xterm.js API compatibility — forked from coder/ghostty-web
CoreCoder
Minimal AI coding agent (~1,000 lines of Python) inspired by Claude Code. Works with any LLM. Think NanoGPT for coding agents. Formerly NanoCoder.
 VTCode
VT Code is a Rust coding agent with LLM-native code understanding, OS-native sandboxing, and multi-provider support.
## What I'm building OmniRoute gives developers one local endpoint for hundreds of AI providers and models. It focuses on resilient routing, transparent fallback, token efficiency, open protocols, and making powerful AI tooling more accessible without hiding operational trade-offs. Since February 2026, it has grown into a project shaped by hundreds of contributors, with multilingual documentation and interface localization. Translation coverage varies by resource; the current project documentation records what is available. My current open-source work includes: - Multi-provider routing and failure recovery. - OpenAI, Anthropic, MCP, and A2A interoperability. - Reproducible free-tier, cost, quota, and token-efficiency methodologies. - Maintainer workflows that preserve contributor credit and keep decisions auditable. - Documentation, support, and contribution paths for a global developer community. ## Start here The architecture, routing, resilience, and contribution links below point to the published v3.8.51 release. The repository's default branch also contains work for the next release. | Resource | What you'll find | | --- | --- | | [OmniRoute](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute) | Source, installation, roadmap, and current project status | | [Architecture](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/blob/v3.8.51/docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md) | Request pipeline and system design | | [Routing](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/blob/v3.8.51/docs/routing/AUTO-COMBO.md) | Multi-provider selection and Auto-Combo methodology | | [Resilience](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/blob/v3.8.51/docs/architecture/RESILIENCE_GUIDE.md) | Provider breakers, connection cooldowns, and model lockouts | | [Contributing](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/blob/v3.8.51/CONTRIBUTING.md) | How to propose, test, and submit a contribution | | [Discussions](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/discussions) | Questions, ideas, feedback, and community support | ## Community I maintain in public, publish the reasoning behind technical decisions, answer questions, and work with contributors to turn real-world feedback into documented, tested improvements. If OmniRoute is useful to you, contributions and thoughtful criticism are both welcome. Recent examples of that work: - [Reviewing and rechecking a contributor's shutdown fixes](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/pull/16033): reproducible feedback, corrections by the original author, and a clear distinction between focused validation and broader CI. - [Working through a user's routing observations](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/discussions/14270): agreeing on focused issues, regression tests, and contributor ownership. - [Restoring credit lost during merges](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/pull/14362): recording the original contributors in project history and release notes. - [Helping a user understand provider controls](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/discussions/14158): a public answer others can reuse.
